To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inverse probability of treatment weight (IPTW) approach is a useful tool for the joint modeling of concurrent binary longitudinal outcomes and (2) the IPTW approach can be used to estimate treatment effect in the presence of time-dependent confounders.

(1) a novel approach to the analysis of binary longitudinal outcomes is to use a generalized mixed model with a random intercept and a random coefficient for time, (2) the use of this model for the analysis of concurrent binary outcomes is complicated by the need for an adjustment for the correlation between outcomes, (3) the adjustment for correlation between outcomes can be achieved using the generalized estimating equations approach, (4) the use of inverse probability of treatment weights can be used to address confounding in the estimation
the inverse probability weighting method can be applied to the longitudinal data and the proposed method is useful in estimating treatment effect for binary outcomes in the longitudinal data.
